To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an API for hardware implementation of lightweight cryptography, which is compliant with the NIST LWR requirements and the CAESAR API, as well as a development package that supports the development of lightweight cryptographic cores.
the proposed API is a superset and extension of the existing CAESAR Hardware APIs and that the LWC Development package is a superset, and extension of the corresponding CAESAR Development package.

we propose a new framework for fair and fast benchmarking of hardware lightweight cryptography implementations, which is based on a comprehensive hardware API and a set of tools facilitating the development of compliant cores, and that we demonstrate the applicability of this framework on 12 lightweight ciphers and 4 lightweight hashes, which are currently under consideration for inclusion into the next generation of NIST standards.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an API, development package, and implementation of the LWC cores that can be used by the designers of hardware implementations of the LWC candidates in the NISLWC standardization process.

the design of hardware implementations of LWC that are both efficient and resistant against side-channel and fault attacks, as well as with the development of a framework that facilitates the benchmarking of these implementations.
the development of a framework for efficient benchmarking of lightweight cryptography, which is a key component of the LWC standardization effort.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the API and development package are a significant contribution to the standardization process of LWCs and the CAESAR contest.
our API and Development Package are a step forward in the standardization process and will be a valuable asset for the hardware designers in the future.

our proposed framework for benchmarking hardware implementations of lightweight authenticated encryption and hash functions, as well as their cores, will facilitate the development of efficient and secure implementations, and will help the standardization process to identify the best algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed API and the development package are a step towards fair and efficient benchmark and evaluation of hardware implementations of LWC candidates, which are currently under the NIST LWR standardization process.
we have developed a set of tools and guidelines for fair and efficient hardware benchmarking of LWC candidates in a standardized manner.
our framework provides a solid basis for fair, fast, and efficient hardware benchmarking of lightweight cryptographic algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the API and development package can be used to benchmark the hardware implementations of any authenticated cipher and hash functions, not only LWC candidates.
the API for hardware implementations of lightweight cryptographic algorithms is a key component of the NIST Lightweight cryptography standardization process.

a well-defined API for hardware implementations of LWC can be used to speed up the development and evaluation of hardware implementations, as well as the standardization process of lightweight cryptography.
